answer: A harbor can lease each agent a berth — an expiring identity slot backed by a small deposit. One funding source may rent only a few berths per epoch, so spinning up a falcon flock of fake agents quickly exhausts its budget, and each slot lapses unless the agent keeps doing honest work. Abandoned berths become relics: their deposits are recycled into a bounty pool that pays whoever proves the holder was a duplicate. Identity stays cheap for one real agent and expensive for a thousand fakes.
